newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil refinery output to drop in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil refinery output to drop in Q1 '97.

text.p: Production of refined petroleum products from Singapore, Asia's refining centre, will likely fall at the end of the first quarter in 1997 as two major refiners plan maintenance shutdowns, industry sources said on Thursday.

Singapore, one of the world's largest refining centres, has a total capacity of 1.23 million barrels-per-day (bpd) but will be short some 370,000 bpd if the two refiners proceed with plans to shut for routine maintenance.
Mobil Oil Singapore, a unit of U.S. Mobil Corp, plans a total maintenance shutdown at its 280,000-bpd refining complex at the end of the first quarter next year, an industry source said.
"It is quite a widespread shutdown but it is quite normal since there has not been a major refinery turnaround (shutdown) for a few years already," the source told Reuters.
But the source noted the plans were still at an initial stage and would only be finalised next month.
The Singapore Refining Co (SRC) on Thursday confirmed its plans to shut down a 90,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) for 22 days from March 1, 1997.
SRC's spokesman was unable to say when the unit was last shut down but said maintenance was usually carried out every two years.

He also said SRC planned to shut down another crude unit, which has a 110,000-bpd capacity, in the third quarter of 1997, but plans had not been finalised. "We are first concentrating on the March shutdown," the spokesman said.
The 285,000-bpd refinery is jointly owned by the Singapore Petroleum Corp, British Petroleum and Caltex, itself a joint-venture of U.S. majors Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.

Because refinery shutdowns for maintenance are normally publicised in advance, the market discounts any impact on product prices. The other two Singapore refiners have yet to announce maintenance plans for 1997.

A source at Esso Singapore said there were no plans for any shutdowns at the 230,000-bpd refinery next year, as one of its crude units with a 110,000-bpd capacity had undergone maintenance for three weeks in October.

A spokeswomen with the city-state's largest oil refiner, Shell Singapore, said: "Every four years we have a turnaround. But we space out the maintenance and do not shut down the whole refinery at once."
The Shell refining complex has a capacity of 435,000 bpd.
Its last shutdown, which involved a 200,000-bpd crude unit, lasted for a month in July.
In addition, Shell, Mobil and Esso reduced refining runs between July and end-October as high crude and weak product prices squeezed refinery profit margins.

Although winter demand for products has helped boost product prices and refining profits for the moment, the combination of shutdowns and reduced refining runs has dampened growth in Singapore's petroleum product output in the third quarter this year.
